note: Manually curated moves that broke before the scraped feeds caught up. Same shape as transactions.json rows; appended after the feed so a later feed row for the same player supersedes these. Remove entries once the feed carries them.

transactions.detail: Memphis (MEM) fully guaranteed $9 million salary for 2026-27
transactions.why: His offer sheet is reported as 3yr/$30M, which is $26.1M of base plus $1.35M a year of unlikely incentives; the signings feed carries the $26.1M base. Back-solved with standard 5% RAISES that gives a 2026-27 of $8,285,714, but the deal DESCENDS — Spotrac's cap table has him at $9,000,000, and 9.0 + 8.7 + 8.4 is $26.1M exactly, the same total from the other direction. A descending shape is legal (Art. II §5(b) allows an 8% decline) and it is what was filed, so the year-one figure is stated here for STATED_SALARY rather than inferred. Our own resolvedOfferSheetsNote already said 'Y1 $9M guaranteed'; nothing was reading it.

transactions.detail: Waived by Sacramento (SAC) - leaves behind $10 million in dead cap
transactions.why: Sacramento waived him Jul 6 2026 keeping a $10M guarantee, which roster-corrections carried as a waivedFreeAgents entry — a shape that only describes an UNSIGNED waived player. When he signed with Denver on Aug 21 his row moved to DEN with the new minimum and Sacramento's $10M vanished from the league's books entirely. He is now the ACTIVE_LATER case Jonathan Isaac already documents: the old team's charge needs its own dead row beside the new deal, and STATED_DEAD_CAP builds one from a Release row that states the amount. This is that row.

transactions.detail: Waived by Dallas (DAL) via Buyout - leaves behind $7.660317 million in dead cap
transactions.why: He was owed $17,460,317 by Dallas for 2026-27 and gave back $9.8M to get the buyout (ESPN/RealGM, Aug 21), which leaves $7,660,317 dead on the Mavericks' books. Spotrac's row states the buyout but not the amount, so nothing on the sheet charged Dallas anything at all and $17.5M simply vanished from their cap sheet. This row supplies the figure STATED_DEAD_CAP needs. Cross-check: $7,660,317 from Dallas plus his new Miami salary against the $17,460,317 he walked away from is the ~$3.5M net loss the reporting describes.

transactions.detail: Waived by Memphis (MEM) via Buyout - leaves behind $17.744971 million in dead cap
transactions.why: He exercised a $21,621,500 player option Jun 19, then gave back exactly $3,876,529 in the Jul 25 buyout — the 10+ YOS veteran minimum, i.e. precisely what Philadelphia then paid him, making the move net-neutral to the dollar. Memphis carries $17,744,971. The Spotrac row states the buyout but not the amount, so this row supplies the dead-cap figure STATED_DEAD_CAP needs.

transactions.detail: Signed a 1 year $3.876529 million contract with Philadelphia (PHI)
transactions.why: Reported by ESPN/Shams Jul 25 and finalized after he cleared waivers — the 10+ YOS veteran minimum, the same figure he forfeited in Memphis. A ONE-year minimum, so Art. VII §3(f) charges Philadelphia only the 2-YOS minimum ($2,449,421) against the cap and their first-apron hard cap. Not yet in Spotrac's signed-FA feed as of the Jul 28 pull.

transactions.detail: Signed a 1 year $2.845883 million contract with Cleveland (CLE)
transactions.why: ESPN/RealGM Jul 26: first NBA deal since 2019-20 after five EuroLeague seasons. The reported '$2.8M' is the 5-YOS veteran minimum ($2,845,883) — his five NBA seasons were 2015-16 through 2019-20 — NOT the taxpayer MLE, which is more than double at $6,064,000. Booked at the exact minimum so Art. VII §3(f) charges Cleveland the 2-YOS figure. Agreed but not yet in Spotrac's feed as of the Jul 28 pull.
